title: The Satellite That Needed a Plan for Later
title_ja: 任務のあとも考える人工衛星
fact_notes: 学校の活動と衛星計画は架空。本文・和訳・問題は独自制作。

sentences.en: A science class studies how satellites help people communicate and observe Earth from space.
sentences.ja: 理科のクラスは人工衛星が宇宙から通信や地球観測をどう助けるか学びます。

sentences.en: The teacher shows a diagram with many objects traveling around the planet.
sentences.ja: 教師は地球の周りを移動する多くの物体を示す図を見せます。

sentences.en: Some objects are working satellites, while others are pieces left by earlier space activities.
sentences.ja: 一部は活動中の人工衛星ですが、ほかは以前の宇宙活動で残された破片です。

sentences.en: However, students are surprised to learn that an object can remain a concern even after its mission ends.
sentences.ja: しかし使命を終えた後も物体が問題であり続けると知って生徒たちは驚きます。

sentences.en: The class begins to ask who is responsible for keeping shared areas of space usable.
sentences.ja: クラスは宇宙の共有区域を使える状態に保つ責任は誰にあるか問い始めます。

sentences.en: Their project focuses on the choices made before a satellite is launched as well as after it stops working.
sentences.ja: 活動は人工衛星の打ち上げ前と動かなくなった後の選択に焦点を当てます。

sentences.en: Objects traveling in orbit can move at great speeds, making even small fragments worth considering.
sentences.ja: 軌道を移動する物体は非常に速く動くため小さな破片にも注意が必要です。

sentences.en: For example, a fragment that looks harmless in a picture may create a serious problem if it meets another object.
sentences.ja: 例えば写真では無害に見える破片も別の物体に接近すると重大な問題を生むかもしれません。

sentences.en: Students learn that diagrams often simplify distances and sizes so a complicated situation can be shown clearly.
sentences.ja: 生徒たちは複雑な状況を明確に示すため図が距離や大きさを単純化することがあると学びます。

sentences.en: They should therefore avoid treating every drawing as an exact map of where objects actually are.
sentences.ja: そのためすべての図を物体の実際の位置の正確な地図として扱うべきではありません。

sentences.en: The teacher explains that observations and estimates help specialists study risks without proving exactly what will happen next.
sentences.ja: 教師は観察と推定が次に何が起こるかを正確に証明しなくても専門家のリスク研究を助けると説明します。

sentences.en: A careful explanation must distinguish a possible danger from a collision that has already occurred.
sentences.ja: 慎重な説明は起こり得る危険とすでに起きた衝突を区別する必要があります。

sentences.en: The students compare two fictional plans for sending a useful satellite into orbit.
sentences.ja: 生徒たちは役立つ人工衛星を軌道へ送る二つの架空の計画を比べます。

sentences.en: One plan focuses only on what the satellite will accomplish during its main mission.
sentences.ja: 一つの計画は主な任務中に衛星が達成することだけに焦点を当てます。

sentences.en: Instead of considering the mission alone, the other plan also asks what should happen when the satellite can no longer work.
sentences.ja: 任務だけを考える代わりにもう一つの計画は衛星が動かなくなった後をどうするかも問います。

sentences.en: Students discuss why future responsibilities should be considered before a project begins.
sentences.ja: 生徒たちは将来の責任を活動開始前に考えるべき理由を話し合います。

sentences.en: They also consider the cost of monitoring objects and sharing reliable information with other organizations.
sentences.ja: 物体の監視と他の組織への信頼できる情報共有の費用も考慮します。

sentences.en: The group understands that a successful mission today should not create avoidable difficulties for future missions.
sentences.ja: 現在の任務の成功が将来の任務へ避けられる困難を生むべきではないと理解します。

sentences.en: Some students suggest that one country should simply decide how all objects in orbit are managed.
sentences.ja: 生徒の中には一国が軌道上のすべての物体の管理を決めればよいと提案する人もいます。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, the class realizes that many countries and organizations use space for different purposes.
sentences.ja: それでも多くの国と組織が異なる目的で宇宙を利用するとクラスは理解します。

sentences.en: The teacher asks them to consider how information can be shared and responsibilities discussed across borders.
sentences.ja: 教師は国境を越えた情報共有と責任の話し合いの方法を考えるよう求めます。

sentences.en: The students decide that cooperation is necessary even when organizations do not agree on every detail.
sentences.ja: 生徒たちは組織がすべての細部で一致しなくても協力が必要だと考えます。

sentences.en: They avoid claiming that a simple classroom proposal would solve every real-world challenge.
sentences.ja: 単純な教室の提案ですべての現実問題が解決するとは主張しません。

sentences.en: Instead, they identify practical questions that future engineers and decision makers will need to address.
sentences.ja: むしろ将来の技術者や意思決定者が取り組む必要のある実際的な問いを挙げます。

sentences.en: At the final presentation, the class explains the difference between a satellite's immediate benefits and its long-term responsibilities.
sentences.ja: 最終発表でクラスは人工衛星の目先の利点と長期的な責任の違いを説明します。

sentences.en: They display their comparison of the two plans and describe which information is still uncertain.
sentences.ja: 二つの計画の比較を示し、まだ不確かな情報を説明します。

sentences.en: As a result, classmates begin asking questions about the full life of a technology rather than only its exciting beginning.
sentences.ja: その結果、同級生は技術の魅力的な始まりだけでなくその全期間について問い始めます。

sentences.en: The project shows that innovation can be valuable while still requiring care for shared resources.
sentences.ja: この活動は革新には価値があっても共有資源への配慮が必要であることを示します。

sentences.en: Students learn that what happens after a mission can be just as important as the mission itself.
sentences.ja: 生徒たちは任務の後に起きることも任務自体と同じくらい重要だと学びます。

sentences.en: The future of space exploration depends partly on the decisions people make about the objects they leave behind.
sentences.ja: 宇宙探査の未来は人々が残す物体についての決定にも部分的に左右されます。

questions.prompt: What surprises students about space objects?
options: Objects can remain a concern after a mission ends.
Every object stops moving when its mission ends.
Satellite diagrams are always exact maps.
questions.explanation_ja: 第1段落「しかし使命を終えた後も物体が問題であり続けると知って生徒たちは驚きます。」が根拠です。

options: Only the appearance of a rocket.
Choices before launch and after a satellite stops working.
questions.explanation_ja: 第1段落「活動は人工衛星の打ち上げ前と動かなくなった後の選択に焦点を当てます。」が根拠です。

questions.prompt: Why should students be careful with orbit diagrams?
options: They can only display working satellites.
They may simplify true distances and sizes.
questions.explanation_ja: 第2段落「生徒たちは複雑な状況を明確に示すため図が距離や大きさを単純化することがあると学びます。」が根拠です。

questions.prompt: What distinction is important when discussing debris?
options: A possible danger versus a collision that has happened.
A working satellite versus a large planet.
questions.explanation_ja: 第2段落「慎重な説明は起こり得る危険とすでに起きた衝突を区別する必要があります。」が根拠です。

questions.prompt: How does the second fictional plan differ?
options: It considers what happens after the satellite stops working.
It ignores the satellite's main mission.
questions.explanation_ja: 第3段落「任務だけを考える代わりにもう一つの計画は衛星が動かなくなった後をどうするかも問います。」が根拠です。

questions.prompt: What future concern do students identify?
options: Avoiding unnecessary difficulties for later missions.
questions.explanation_ja: 第3段落「現在の任務の成功が将来の任務へ避けられる困難を生むべきではないと理解します。」が根拠です。

questions.prompt: Why is one country's decision insufficient?
options: The class has already solved all technical problems.
Many countries and organizations share the use of space.
Only one country has a satellite.
questions.explanation_ja: 第4段落「それでも多くの国と組織が異なる目的で宇宙を利用するとクラスは理解します。」が根拠です。

questions.prompt: What claim does the class avoid?
options: That its simple proposal solves every real-world challenge.
questions.explanation_ja: 第4段落「単純な教室の提案ですべての現実問題が解決するとは主張しません。」が根拠です。

questions.prompt: How does the project affect classmates?
options: They ask about a technology's entire useful life.
They focus only on exciting launches.
They stop caring about shared resources.
questions.explanation_ja: 第5段落「その結果、同級生は技術の魅力的な始まりだけでなくその全期間について問い始めます。」が根拠です。

options: A satellite mission has no effect after it ends.
A single diagram can predict every future collision.
Cooperation is unnecessary for managing orbiting objects.
Space technology must consider long-term shared responsibilities as well as short-term benefits.
questions.explanation_ja: 第5段落「宇宙探査の未来は人々が残す物体についての決定にも部分的に左右されます。」が根拠です。
